Theorem 3.1 . Suppose Assumptions 2.1 – 2.3 hold. There exist constants $\alpha>0$ and $C_{\star}\geq 1$ , depending only on $p$ and $\ell_{f},\ell_{g},\rho_{1},\mu,B_{f},L_{p},\sigma$ , such that the following holds. Run Algorithm 1 from fixed $x_{0},y_{0}$ and $z_{0}=0$ , with $R_{z}=4B_{f}/\mu$ , $\eta_{y}=\eta_{z}=1/(2\ell_{g})$ , and $\eta_{x}=\alpha$ . For any $0<\tau\leq 1$ and positive integers $m,K$ , the output satisfies $\mathbb{E}\|\nabla\Phi(x_{R})\|^{2}\leq C_{\star}\left(\frac{\Delta_{0}}{K}+\tau^{2p}+\frac{1}{m\tau^{2}}\right).$ (18) With the parameter choices in ( 17 ), we obtain $\mathbb{E}\|\nabla\Phi(x_{R})\|^{2}\leq{\epsilon}^{2}$ using at most $(2p+5)mK=\mathcal{O}\!\left({\epsilon}^{-4-2/p}\right)$ oracle calls, for any fixed finite $p$ .

Proposition 4.2 (Bilevel gradient and primitive variance) . For each pair in Proposition 4.1 , every ${\epsilon}\leq\delta\leq 1$ , and sufficiently small ${\epsilon}$ , the family ( 25 ) satisfies Assumption 2.1 with uniformly bounded constants, has $\Phi_{\delta}(0)-\inf\Phi_{\delta}\leq 1$ and $|y_{\delta}^{\star}(0)|\leq 1$ , and obeys $\sup_{x}\|\nabla\Phi_{\delta}(x)-\nabla P(x)\|\leq C_{\rm lift}{\epsilon}^{5}/\delta^{2}\leq C_{\rm lift}{\epsilon}^{3}$ (27) for a numerical $C_{\rm lift}>0$ . The oracle ( 26 ) is conditionally unbiased, has joint variance at most $C_{\rm lift}\delta^{2}{\epsilon}^{2}/\varpi$ , and is simulated by one call to $\mathcal{R}_{\varpi}$ .

Theorem 4.3 (Lower bound for bilevel problems) . There exist numerical constants $M_{0}\geq 1$ , $c>0$ , and ${\epsilon}_{0}>0$ such that the following holds for every integer $p\geq 1$ and $0<{\epsilon}<{\epsilon}_{0}$ . For any adaptive randomized algorithm using at most $c{\epsilon}^{-4-2/p}$ primitive oracle calls, there is a pair in $\mathcal{P}_{p}(M_{0})$ on which its output satisfies $\mathbb{E}\|\nabla\Phi(x_{\rm out})\|^{2}>{\epsilon}^{2}.$ (31)

Proposition A.8 (A uniform one-step inequality) . Under Assumptions 2.1 – 2.3 and the step choices ( 37 ), for every $\tau>0$ and positive integer $m$ , $\mathbb{E}_{k}\mathcal{V}_{k+1}\leq\mathcal{V}_{k}-\frac{\alpha}{4}\|\nabla\Phi(x_{k})\|^{2}-\alpha CT_{k}+\alpha S_{\rm b}\beta^{2}+\alpha S_{\rm v}v.$ (68) All constants are given in Appendix A.1 ; in particular, the step sizes do not depend on the target accuracy.

Corollary B.3 (Two-vector probability- $\varpi$ zero-chain) . For any $\varpi\in(0,1]$ , let $\zeta\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\varpi)$ and define $a^{(1)}(v,\zeta):=\nabla B_{T}(v),\qquad a^{(2)}(v,\zeta):=\frac{\zeta}{\varpi}\nabla W_{T}(v).$ Then, simultaneously for every $v$ , $\max_{\ell\in\{1,2\}}\operatorname{prog}_{0}(a^{(\ell)}(v,\zeta))\leq\operatorname{prog}_{1/4}(v)+1,$ and on the event $\{\zeta=0\}$ , $\max_{\ell\in\{1,2\}}\operatorname{prog}_{0}(a^{(\ell)}(v,\zeta))\leq\operatorname{prog}_{1/4}(v).$ The exceptional event is independent of $v$ and has probability $\varpi$ .

Corollary B.14 (Terminal output) . Under the assumptions of Lemma B.13 , suppose $d>N+1+T$ and, after $N$ calls, the algorithm outputs an $\sigma(\xi_{0},\mathcal{T}_{N})$ -measurable point $x_{\rm out}$ with $\left\lVert x_{\rm out}\right\rVert\leq R$ . Then $\displaystyle\mathbb{P}\left(\max\left\{\max_{t\leq N}\operatorname{prog}_{1/4}(U^{\top}x_{t}),\operatorname{prog}_{1/4}(U^{\top}x_{\rm out})\right\}\geq T\right)$ $\displaystyle\qquad\leq e^{2\varpi N-T}+2(N+1)T\exp\!\left(-\frac{d-(N+1)-T}{32R^{2}(N+1)}\right).$ (146)

Corollary B.15 (Soft projection and known postprocessing) . Let $\rho:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be Borel with $\left\lVert\rho(x)\right\rVert\leq R$ for all $x$ . Let $(x,y,o)\mapsto\mathsf{P}_{x,y}(o)$ be a jointly Borel map independent of $U$ , and suppose the actual response is $\mathsf{P}_{x,y}\!\left(\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}_{U}(\rho(x),y;\xi)\right).$ Then Lemma B.13 and Corollary B.14 hold with $U^{\top}x$ replaced by $U^{\top}\rho(x)$ .
